props.title: Inserts

sections.content: **Inserts** (1975) stands as one of the most daring explorations of Hollywood's underbelly, directed by John Byrum in his debut. This meta-commentary stars Richard Dreyfuss as a washed-up silent film director who's reduced to making pornographic "inserts" in 1930s Hollywood. It's a direct predecessor to Paul Thomas Anderson's **Boogie Nights** (1997), sharing its unflinching look at the adult film industry, though Inserts takes place during a pivotal moment when silent cinema was dying and sound changed everything.

movies.title: Sunset Boulevard
movies.slug: Gloria Swanson plays a forgotten silent film star unable to accept that her era has ended

sections.content: The film's claustrophobic setting - entirely within one house - mirrors similar chamber pieces about Hollywood's dark side like **Whatever Happened to Baby Jane?** (1962). Dreyfuss delivers a tour-de-force performance as "Boy Wonder," a director who once worked with the greats but now can barely leave his mansion, reflecting real stories of silent era directors like Oscar Micheaux who struggled to transition to sound.

What makes **Inserts** (1975) particularly remarkable is its X-rating (now NC-17) despite featuring established actors like Dreyfuss and Veronica Cartwright. It follows in the tradition of serious adult-themed films like **Last Tango in Paris** (1972) and predates the wave of Hollywood films about pornography like **Hardcore** (1979) and **Star 80** (1983). SUBHEAD: Hollywood's Self-Reflection

movies.title: The Artist
movies.slug: A modern silent film about a star struggling with the transition to talkies

sections.content: The film belongs to a distinct category of movies about moviemaking that expose the industry's seedier aspects, alongside works like **The Day of the Locust** (1975) and **Mulholland Drive** (2001). These films strip away Hollywood glamour to reveal the desperate struggles of those on the margins of the entertainment industry.
